Hello can you tell me about Kazakhstan I have never heard of them

Absolutely! Kazakhstan is located in the middle of Eurasia. It is officially known as the Republic of Kazakhstan. It is the ninth biggest country in the world, and it has been inhabited since the Paleolithic era. It is the largest landlocked country in the world.
Wow the largest landlocked country in world. How is the culture there?
A Hollywood director named Timur Bekmambetov is originally from Kazakhstan, and he is trying to bridge the gap between Hollywood and the Kazakhstan film industry.
hmmm, tell me more

Kazakhstan's Olympic performance was assessed to be on of the best in the world during the last three Olympic games. They had more medals than any country in the world with the exception of Cuba and Russia.
Do you know what the name stands for
Sorry. I don't have that information; however, while the term Kazakhs used to only refer to ethnic Kazakhs it is now increasingly being used to refer to any inhabitant of Kazakhstan.
Do you have any fun facts you would like to share
Natascha Ragosina (while she represented Russia, she is actually from Karaganda) held seven versions of the women's super middleweight title and two heavyweight titles during her career in boxing.
Omg that's impressive, what else can you tell me about Natascha Ragosina
I don't know much more about her, but I do know that she is the longest-reigning WBA female super middleweight champion.
Great information, thank you!
Can I answer anymore questions for you today?
I'm interested in Denmark, what can you tell me about their economy?
Sure thing. With Norway and Sweden, Denmark is part of the Scandinavian Airlines flag carrier. Denmark has a developed mixed economy that is classed as a high-income economy by the World Bank.
Wow, that's amazing! What other interesting information can you tell me about Denmark's economy?

Denmark's largest export partners are Germany, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and the United States. As a result of its acclaimed flexicurity model, Denmark has the freest labour market in Euppe, according to the World Bank.
That's interesting, I didn't know they would have the freest labour market. I would like to know about their demographics now.

Sorry, I don't have any information about their demographics at this time, however, I can tell you more about their economy. Like other Nordic countries, Denmark has adopted the Nordic Model, which combines free-market capitalism with a comprehensive welfare state and strong worker protection. Today, Denmark is part of the European Union's internal market, which represents more than 508 million consumers.
Okay, I would like to learn about their geography.

Sorry, I don't have any information about their geography at this time, however, I just found some information about their Demographics. Overall, the net migration rate in 2017 was 2.1 migrant /1,000 population, somewhat lower than the United Kingdom and the other Nordic countries. This places Denmark above the OECD average and above the other Nordic countries.
Thanks for that, do you know what Denmark is known for?
I do! Denmark is known for its Carisberg and Tuborg beers and for its akvavit and bitters.
Interesting, thanks for all the information.
You're welcome!
Good evening, Uttarakhand sounds like a unique name, what can you tell me about it?
Hello! Uttarakhand is a state of India in the north region. It shares a border with China that is in dispute.
Really can you tell me more about this subdivision
Sure! Uttarakhand is divided into two divisions, Kumaon and Garhwal, which contain a total of 13 districts.
Can you tell me anything else
I do not have more information about the subdivisions, but Uttarakhand has a multi-ethnic population spread across all districts.

Of course. Vasant Panchami is a festival that marks the arrival of spring and some festivals and musical affairs can last up to a month.
Can you tell me more?
Sure! In Uttarakhand, hundreds of foreigners join Indian pilgrims in some festivals that are considered the largest religious gatherings in the world.
Thank you so much for the information.

Hi there, it would be my pleasure. Kyrgyzstan, formally the Kyrgyz Republic and sometime known as Kirghizia, is a landlocked and mountainous country in Central Asia. Its capital is Bishkek.
What can you tell me about its economy?
Well, Kyrgyzstan was the 8th poorest country in the former Soviet Union, and today is the second poorest country in Central Asia after Tajikistan.
Oh, that's sad. What else is interesting about economics there?

Unfortunately, I don't have access to any economy facts right now but I am happy to tell you that Kyrgyzstan is one of the 2 former Soviet republics in Central Asia to have Russian as an official language, Kazakhstan being the other.
Okay. Can you tell me their political arena?
Their political arena is similar to other countries as it's judicial branch comprises a Supreme Court, local courts and a Chief Prosecutor.
Alright. Any other political info?
The Agency of National Security works with the military and serves similar purposes to its Soviet predecessor, the KGB.
Thanks. Any last funfm facts maybe about politics or even education?

It's not a fun fact but one that is important to recognize is the fact that at the moment, different political groups are fighting for power in the republic and 3 of the 75 elected members of Parliament have been murdered.
I appreciate the thoughtful response. That's all I needed today.
Thank you for your time chatting with me. Have a great day!
Hi! Would you please tell me about the geography of Norway?
Hello! Sure! Norway lies between latitudes 57° and 81°N, and longitudes 4° and 32°E. Norway is the northernmost of the Nordic countries and if Svalbard is included also the easternmost.
Are there a lot of mountains there and is Norway where the fjords are?

Unfortunately, I don't have information about the mountains or fjords in Norway but I can tell you more about Norway's geography. You may find this interesting; Norway's core territory comprises the western and northernmost portion of the Scandinavian Peninsula; the remote island of Jan Mayen and the archipelago of Svalbard are also part of the Kingdom of Norway.
I didn't realize it was so big! What other countries border it?

The mainland of Norway is surrounded by the North Sea and Atlantic Ocean on the west side, and borders Russia, Finland, and Sweden to the east. The southern coast touches the Oslofjord, Skagerrak, and the North Sea.
That is interesting. I didn't know it reached all the way to the Atlantic. So, you said Norway is a kingdom. It must be a very old country. Do you know how its name originated?

The English name Norway comes from the Old English word "Norþweg" mentioned in 880, meaning "northern way" or "way leading to the north", which is how the Anglo-Saxons referred to the coastline of Atlantic Norway similar to scientific consensus about the origin of the Norwegian language name.
Do you know who the native peoples were?

I'm sorry, I don't have that specific information but I can tell you a bit of history regarding King Charles III John. King Charles III John, who came to the throne of Norway and Sweden in 1818, was the second king following Norway's break from Denmark and the union with Sweden.
I didn't realize those three countries were part of one at one time. Interesting. One last question, please. What languages were or are spoken there?

Sure! Norwegian is the national language. However, there are two official written versions of Norwegian called "Bokmål" and "Nynorsk". Also, the Northern Sami language is spoken by around 90% of those who speak one of Norway's 3 Sami languages. Northern Sami is also an official language in a number of municipalities.
Thank you for the interesting conversation tonight. I learned a lot!

Ponce has the highest concentration of medical infrastructure per inhabitant of any municipality in Puerto Rico

Founded in 1956, it is operated by the Medical Services Administration of the Department of Health of Puerto Rico, and is actually a network of eight hospitals.

There is also a U.S Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic that provides health services in U.S verternas.
So obviously the people's health and safety it's pretty good in Puerto Rico how about their education?
As of 2002, the literacy rate of the Puerto Rican population was 94.1%; by gender, it was 93.9% for males and 94.4% for females.
So obviously the people's health and safety it's pretty good in Puerto Rico how about their education?
what else can i tell you

The largest private university systems on the island are the Sistema Universitario Ana G. Mendez which operates the Universidad del Turabo Metropolitain University and Universidad del Este

I do not have that information, but i can tell you that on the island of Culebra, there is a small hospital in the island called Hospital de Culebra

you are very welcome. Can i help with anything else?

messages.message: Hello! what can you tell me about the Latin American country Costa Rica?
This central American country is bordered by Micaragua to the north, Panama to the southeast, the Pacific ocean to the west and the Carribean Sea to the east. The official language is spanish there.
Interesting, can you tell me more about Panama?
I am not sure about Panama, but Costa Rica was the point where the Mesoamaerican and South American native cultures met.
No problem, can you tell me about the Education ?
Sure, Students who finish 11th grade receive a Costa Rican Bachillerato Diploma accredited by The Costa Rican Ministry of Education.
What can you tell me about the Ministry of Education?
Well a 2016 report by the U.S. Government report identifies the current challengesfacing the education system is the dropout rate among high school students.
That is certainly an issue. Can you tell me anything about the culture?
yes, The northwest of the country, the Nicoya pennisula, was the most southernmost point of Nahuati cultural influence when the spanish conquistadores came in the 16th century.
What can you tell me about the Conquistadores?
Not much on hand but I can tell you Costa Rica was sparsely inhabited by indeigenous people before coming under spanish rule in the 16th century.
Thanks the country has a Rich History. Thank you that is all that i needed to know for today.
Anytime!
The US Virgin Islands are a place I need to know more about. What knowledge could you share with me?

The United States Virgin Islands is a group of islands in the Caribbean and an unincorporated and organized territory of the United States. Like other territories, the U.S. Virgin Islands does not have U.S. Senators.

I was pretty sure about where they are geographically, but not I know for sure. The part about the senators is something I didn't know however. Does that mean that the territory has no representatives to the government of the US?

Sorry, I do not know the exact answer to that, however, I can tell you a little about their history. The United States took possession of the islands on March 31st, 1917 and that was the same time that it was renamed to Virgin Islands of the United States.
How is the government structured? I don't know much about how a territory of the US differs from a state.

The main political parties in the U.S. Virgin Islands are the Democratic Party of the Virgin Islands, the Independent Citizens Movement, and the Republican Party of the Virgin Islands. Although they are US citizens, US Virgin Islanders residing in the territory are ineligible to vote for the President of the United States.
Do you happen to know who the current head of the government of the US Virgin Islands is?

Sorry, I do not know that exact answer, however, I can tell you some more facts about the politics and government in general. The US Democratic and Republican parties allow U.S. Virgin Islands citizens to vote in their presidential primary elections for delegates to the respective national conventions. People born in the U.S. Virgin Islands derive their US citizenship from Congressional statute.
I had no idea, wow. What about the culture there? Is it much different from the mainland US?

The culture derives chiefly from West African, European, and American cultures, in addition to the influences from the immigrants from the Arab world, India, and other Caribbean islands. Virgin Islands government employees are also given administrative leave for St. Croix carnival events in January and St. Thomas carnival events in April/May.
Sounds like a cultural potpourri. In what way does the Arab world influence the culture there?

Sorry, I don't have any information on that, but I could tell you a little more about their culture. The islands have a number of AM and FM radio stations (which are mostly on St. Thomas and St.Croix) which broadcasts music, religion, and news programming. Full and low-power television stations are split between St. Thomas and St. Croix.
That'

Here are some more Politics and government facts for you. Estate names are still used to write addresses; estates and quarters are used in describing real estate, especially on St. John and St. Croix. Each of the 3 main islands on the U.S. Virgin Islands is counted as a county-equivalent by the U.S. Census Bureau, with the following FIPS codes, 78010 for Saint Croix, 78020 for Saint John, and 78030 for Saint Thomas.
That's all very helpful. Thank you for helping me out.
You're very welcome!
